# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 71 (Bi-Vb Pc71)

**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc71
**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 71
**Title (English, from literature):** Ordaining an unmarried woman under twenty
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul7.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 71 (*Ūnavīsativassa-kumāribhūta*) addresses the improper ordination of young unmarried women within the Theravāda Vinaya. According to the rule, a nun incurs an offense requiring confession (*pācittiya*) if she ordains an unmarried girl (*kumāribhūtā*) who is under twenty years of age [Bodhi, Revival of Bhikkhunī Ordination; Hüsken 1997]. Bhikkhu Bodhi observes that unlike certain other ordination procedures, this rule admits no variations regarding whether an act is perceived as legal or illegal; because the candidate is under twenty, any such ordination is deemed inherently invalid [Bodhi, Revival of Bhikkhunī Ordination]. Ute Hüsken contextualizes the rule within a sequence of regulations (Pācittiyas 65–73) that systematically distinguish between formerly married women (*gihigatā*) and unmarried maidens (*kumāribhūtā*), establishing twenty years as a strict minimum age requirement before probation (*sikkhamānā*) and subsequent full ordination are permitted [Hüsken 1997].

Within the Pali canon, DharmaNexus records widespread passage-sharing with closely related nun's ordination rules—particularly Pācittiyas 65, 72, 73, and 74—as well as the corresponding monk's ordination rule in Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 65 and discourses in the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* [DharmaNexus].
